title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1LC0RA_1LD0RC_1LE1LF_1LA0LC_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1LC0RA_1LD0RC_1LE1LF_1LA0LC_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine is a macro machine on lists of numbers: the tape at the left end is A>1 (10)^N sep (10)^w1 sep … (10)^wk sep W, and one sweep takes the fuel N to N−2 and rewrites the start of W by one of a dozen local rules. Lean (kernel) proves such a sweep, with the done blocks w1…wk arbitrary (any number, any values ≥ 2), for the window rules that carry the run; the machine has no halting move inside them. The full list of rules (py/mac14.py) is checked against the machine for 2·107 steps sweep by sweep and at all 33 refills up to 1010 steps, and runs 187,450 sweeps without meeting a case it does not cover. Not proved: the rare fuel-1 sweep and windows with small values, and above all that the run never leaves the rules.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: The cell pieces of a sweep
claims.text: Leaving the left end (start_s, start_z), crossing a done block going right (rb) and coming back (lbA, lbD for values ≥ 4, lb3A … lb2D for 3 and 2), the end at the left (endA_s … endD_0), 14 window rules and the pair rule on the fuel block, each for every value of its counts and every tape around it. Written by bbtools.symtm.prove.

claims.title: One sweep over any list of done blocks
claims.text: sweep_gen: for fuel n+3, any list of done blocks of values ≥ 2 and any window rule that turns back in state A, the machine goes from cfg (n+3) ds W to cfg (n+1) ds W'. sweep_gen2 (fuel 2 → 0) and sweep_gen0 (fuel 0: refilled to 2) likewise. Proved by induction over the list (rpass, lpass).

claims.title: The window rules
claims.text: With fuel ≥ 3 and any done blocks: the pair rule x s y → x+4 s̅ y−1 (pair_dot, pair_bang), append, p1_bd, p1_bb, p1_db, p1_dd (two blocks merge), merge, end_db, next, end_b, restart2; and the pair rule on the fuel block itself (own_dot, own_bang, with step counts).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 80,103 cells have been visited and 39,938 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The macro machine agrees with the machine
claims.text: py/check.py 2e7 checks every one of the sweeps of the first 2·107 steps against the macro rules. py/r14.c prints the tape at every refill (fuel 0) up to 1010 steps; py/cmp.py finds the macro machine equal to it at all 33 of them (74,633 sweeps).

claims.title: 187,450 sweeps inside the rules
claims.text: py/far.py runs the macro machine 187,450 sweeps (far past 1010 machine steps) and never meets a window or fuel case that its rules do not cover.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof would need an invariant on the lists that the macro rules preserve (so that no window ever falls outside them), plus Lean proofs of the remaining cases: the sweep with fuel 1 (two rules in one visit), the windows with small values, and the rules on the fuel block other than the pair rule.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape turns out to be a list of numbers, written as blocks of 10s, with a fuel counter at the left end. Each sweep of the head spends 2 units of fuel and does one small piece of arithmetic at the first unfinished block; when the fuel runs out, a finished block becomes the new fuel. Lean proves the sweep exactly; the rules have run 187,450 sweeps without a gap.

facts.text: Exact, for any list of done blocks and 12 window rules (Lean).
The macro machine equals the real run at all 33 refills.
The macro rules never meet a case they do not cover.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 80,103 cells (49,545 left of the start, 733 right), with a density of 1s of 0.499.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: The tape is a list of numbers
html: Watch the tape whenever the head, in state A, stands on the leftmost visited cell, on a 1. Read from there, the tape is blocks of 10 separated by single cells: a list v0 s1 v1 s2 v2 … of numbers (how many 10s) and separators (. for 0, ! for 1). The first number is a fuel counter N. Then come done blocks, each followed by the 5-cell separator 0 1 1 0 0 (. 0 ! 1 . in the list), and then the window, the first block that is not done:

sections.heading: One sweep: fuel −2, one rule at the window
html: From the left end the head runs right in state B. It crosses each done block, leaving it in a temporary form ((10)^w sep becomes (01)^(w−1) 1010101), does a few dozen steps of work at the window, and turns back in state A. On the way back it puts every block back, two cells further left, and at the left end the fuel has dropped by 2. The commonest rule is the pair rule: x s y → x+4 s̅ y−1 (the separator flips):

sections.heading: A dozen local rules
html: What happens at the window depends only on its first few entries (x is the value there):

windowbecomesLean
x s y, y ≥ 2x+4 s̅ y−1pair_dot, pair_bang
x ! 1 . / x ! 1 !x+4 . 0 . / x+4 . 0 !p1_bd, p1_bb
x . 1 !x+4 ! 0 !p1_db
x . 1 . zx+5+zp1_dd
x ! 0 ! z .x+4+z .merge
x . 0 . zx done, window 1 ! znext
x . 0 . 0 . 0 ! 1 .x done, window 2 ! 1 .restart2
x sep 1 ! 0 at the endx sep 2 sep 1 ! 0append
x ! 0 / x . 0 ! 0 at the endx+1 done, 1 ! 0 / x+4 ! 0end_b, end_db

When the window is the fuel block itself, its own pair rule runs (own_dot, own_bang). When the fuel is 0, the sweep refills it: the list 0 sep v1 … becomes 2 . v1 …, so the first done block joins the fuel (sweep_gen0). Fuel 1 is a special case where one visit applies two rules; that case is not yet proved in Lean.

sections.heading: Carries and powers of four
html: Each refill turns the leftmost done block into fuel, and the fuel pays for pair rules that multiply the window by about 4 while counting its neighbour down. Many of the done blocks that result have the form 4k−2 (2, 14, 62, 254, 1022, 4094, 16382, …), and long runs of 2-blocks pile up at the right end. The list at the refills (computed by the macro machine; the step numbers are from the C run):

The run is like an odometer with irregular digits: the big blocks on the left grow by factors of 4, the short blocks on the right accumulate, and carries ripple through the middle. Every refill so far has been followed by enough work to reach the next refill; nobody has a proof that this always happens.

sections.heading: What is proved and what is missing
html: Lean, kernel: the cell pieces of a sweep (lean/Rules.lean, written by bbtools.symtm), one whole sweep for any done blocks and the window rules above (lean/Macro.lean).
Computed: the full macro machine (py/mac14.py) checked against the machine sweep by sweep for 2·107 steps and at every refill up to 1010; 187,450 sweeps without leaving its rules.

Missing: the fuel-1 sweep, small-value windows and the other fuel-block rules in Lean; a statement that puts all rules together as one map on lists; and an invariant showing the lists always stay inside the rules. Halting would need a window outside every rule; inside the rules proved in Lean the machine never reaches the halting move F1.

family: Counter with fuel (sweeps over a list of blocks; carries like base-4 arithmetic)
summary: The tape is a list of blocks of 10s; each sweep spends 2 units of a fuel counter on the left and applies one local rule at the first unfinished block. Lean proves one sweep exactly for any list of finished blocks and 12 window rules; the macro machine matches the real run to 10<sup>10</sup> steps and runs 187,450 sweeps without leaving its rules.
